Repo: /home/yamal/projects/almanac — AlmanacCore is a platform-free Swift package (SQLite-backed, iOS 17/macOS 14 min) with a companion native iOS app at Native/Almanac.xcodeproj. I need a concrete, file-level implementation plan for two combined efforts (they're really one feature — hydration tracking — split across the core library and the app):

EFFORT A — "Enhance AlmanacCore further":
- Performance: query caching, index optimization
- Testing: edge cases (DST, leap years, timezones)
- Resilience: offline queue, sync recovery
- Integrations: HealthKit completion, Nutrition API

EFFORT B — "Add SwiftUI app target to AlmanacCore package":
- Create iOS app target
- Build: HydrationLoggingView, HydrationDashboardView, SettingsView
- Connect to HydrationLoggingService
- Add HealthKit integration
- Wire up local notifications

=== VERIFIED CURRENT STATE (from three Explore agents, trust this over assumptions) ===

**No hydration code exists at all** — zero hits for "hydration" anywhere except an unrelated chemistry comment. This is a from-scratch module in both AlmanacCore and the app.

**The iOS app target already exists**: Native/Almanac.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj is a real, valid, hand-authored Xcode project. One target `Almanac` (com.apple.product-type.application), iOS 17 deployment target, SUPPORTED_PLATFORMS iphoneos+iphonesimulator, SWIFT_VERSION 5.0, GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE=YES (no physical Info.plist — build-setting-driven), no entitlements file, no HealthKit keys, no notification keys. It consumes AlmanacCore via XCLocalSwiftPackageReference (relativePath="..", i.e. the repo root Package.swift), NOT via a Package.swift app-executable target (SwiftPM can't produce signed .app bundles anyway — confirmed no iOSApplication product type exists in SwiftPM 5.9). Four existing SwiftUI files, all Laboratory-only, all `import AlmanacCore`:
  - Native/Almanac/AlmanacApp.swift — @main App struct; `LaboratoryModel: ObservableObject` (@MainActor) owns Database/LabStore/LabCatalogStore, opens SQLite at Application Support/Almanac/almanac.sqlite, runs migrations, seeds catalog. Also holds shared helpers: EditorFailure, optionalText, dateLabel, readable, View.editorError(_:) modifier, PartialDateFields/editedDate (explicit-precision date entry pattern) — these are reusable by hydration views.
  - Native/Almanac/ReportViews.swift, ResultEditor.swift, HistoryViews.swift — Laboratory CRUD/history UI (patterns to mirror for Hydration views' structure/style, not to modify).
  - No CI exists anywhere in the repo (no .github, no other CI config) — all verification has been manual (Linux `swift build`/`swift test`, `swiftc -frontend -parse` for Native files; **no change has ever actually been run on an Apple platform / Xcode / Simulator**, per docs/implementation-status.md). A Mac + Xcode is required to actually build/run the app target; this plan will be executed/verified by someone with Xcode access, not on this Linux box.
  - Native/README.md documents the build command and states "no HealthKit capability or document picker" for the current scope.

**AlmanacCore layout** (Sources/AlmanacCore/): Backup/, Documents/, Health/ (HealthProvider protocol seam, HealthSampleStore, HealthSyncService), Laboratory/ (9 files, richest module — revisioning, SourceOrdering conflict resolution, catalog matching), Nutrition/ (NutritionCatalog read API, NutritionReferenceImporter — imports a bundle built by the separate Python tool tools/nutrition/almanac_nutrition, GeneralAtwater energy calc), Persistence/ (Database thin SQLite wrapper, MigrationRunner, 10 numbered migrations, currently through Migration011 per one agent / "011" cited — verify exact latest number before adding a new migration), Provenance/, Sync/SyncAnchorStore.swift, Time/ (Clock/SystemClock/FixedClock, PartialDateTime/PartialDateTimeSpan, TimeModel), Timeline/ (Timeline merges per-module TimelineProviding feeds).

**Performance**: NO caching exists anywhere (grep for "cache"/"Cache" = zero hits). Data access is raw SQL per-module struct (LabStore, HealthSampleStore, etc.) directly over Database (thin wrapper: query/run/execute/transaction). Indexing is ad hoc, one CREATE INDEX per migration as needed (idx_lab_observation_time, idx_health_sample_domain_time, idx_nutrition_food_name_fold, idx_nutrition_log_time, idx_nutrition_log_food, idx_nutrition_portion_lookup, idx_backup_manifest_created_at). LabStore.entries(from:to:) has an explicit code comment flagging that range-filtering happens in Swift, not SQL, as a known future optimization (Sources/AlmanacCore/Laboratory/LabStore.swift ~line 936).

**Resilience / offline queue / sync recovery — strong reusable patterns already exist**, don't invent new ones:
  - Sources/AlmanacCore/Sync/SyncAnchorStore.swift — generic domain-keyed opaque-token anchor (`SyncAnchor{domain,token,lastSynced,lastError}`, `load/save/recordFailure`); recordFailure never clears the last-good anchor, so retries resume rather than skip/restart.
  - Sources/AlmanacCore/Health/HealthSyncService.swift — syncOnce(): reads from provider OUTSIDE a transaction, writes rows + advances anchor INSIDE one db.transaction{} — so a write failure leaves the anchor untouched (nothing skipped). This is the template for "offline queue drains, applies, commits its own cursor."
  - Sources/AlmanacCore/Laboratory/LabSourceOrdering.swift + LabStore.upsertReport (LabStore.swift ~143-360) — SourceOrdering enum (.unavailable/.sequence(Int)/.issuedAt(String)) with compare(to:) returning nil when unrankable (never guesses); LabReportOutcome (.created/.unchanged/.updated/.replayIgnored/.staleIgnored/.conflict); UnrankedImportPolicy (.applyAndFlag/.holdAsConflict) as an injected policy; resolveReportConflict(id:accept:actor:reason:) requires non-empty actor/reason for audit. Fingerprinting (SHA256) distinguishes resent-identical vs genuinely-new vs replay-of-old-version — exactly what's needed to dedupe an offline queue retrying after a dropped network call.
  - Test templates: Tests/AlmanacCoreTests/ImportOrderingTests.swift (testStaleReimportDoesNotBecomeCurrent, testExplicitRevertWithNewerOrderingIsAppliedNotTreatedAsReplay, testOlderOrderedVersionIsIgnored, testOrderingKindsMustMatchToRank), RequestedFixTests.swift (conflict accept/reject with audit), SyncAndBackupTests.swift's testFailureKeepsLastGoodAnchor.

**HealthKit integration — protocol seam exists, needs completion, not creation**:
  - Sources/AlmanacCore/Health/HealthProvider.swift — `protocol HealthProvider { requestAuthorisation(for:); changes(in:since:) -> HealthChangeSet }`, `enum HealthDomain { sleep, workouts, activeEnergy, restingEnergy, steps, heartRate, hrv, bodyMass }` (NO water/hydration case), `FakeHealthProvider` test double. Doc comment explicitly says: "The concrete HealthKitProvider belongs in the iOS target and is the only place `import HealthKit` may appear."
  - Sources/AlmanacCore/Health/HealthSampleStore.swift — only `.bodyMass` domain is actually wired up/tested; table itself is domain-agnostic.
  - HealthProvider is READ-ONLY (changes(in:since:)) — logging hydration and pushing it TO HealthKit needs either a new write method on the protocol or a separate writer seam.
  - No concrete HealthKitProvider iOS adapter exists yet anywhere — this genuinely needs to be written in Native/, per the doc's explicit intent.

**Nutrition API**: tools/nutrition/almanac_nutrition is a separate Python build-time pipeline (produces a SQLite bundle), not a runtime API. Package.swift has no separate Nutrition target — it's a subfolder of the single AlmanacCore target. Runtime integration point: NutritionReferenceImporter.importBundle(at:) (ATTACHes + copies verified rows transactionally, re-verifies licence/qualifiers in Swift via BundleGuard rather than trusting the bundle blindly). Read API: NutritionCatalog (food(_:), values(for:basis:), bases(for:), energy(for:basis:), search(_:limit:)). There IS a nutrition_log migration (Migration009: food-eaten logging, grams/quantity, eaten_at+precision+tz columns, soft-delete, one revision table) but NO Swift store/service was ever built on top of it — this is a gap parallel to hydration, and nutrition_log's schema shape (source_system/external_id identity, *_at/*_precision/*_tz_offset_minutes/*_tz_id columns, soft deleted_at, single revision table) is the closest existing template for how hydration_log should look.

**Testing patterns**: XCTest only (no Swift Testing). 115 existing tests. Naming: testDescriptiveSentenceCase(). Fixture pattern: private fixture()/migrated() helper builds Database.inMemory(), runs MigrationRunner(migrations: AlmanacMigrations.all).migrate(db), constructs store under test with FixedClock. On-disk DB tests use NSTemporaryDirectory()+UUID, clean up .sqlite/-wal/-shm in tearDown. Clock protocol (SystemClock/FixedClock with advance(by:)) is injected everywhere instead of bare Date() — only 2 direct Date() calls in all of production code, both are defaulted-parameter fallbacks, not hardcoded bypasses. TimeModel wraps Calendar with explicit injected TimeZone + DayBoundary (.midnight/.wakeOffset(hours:)), computes day bounds via calendar.date(byAdding:.day...) NOT +86400s specifically so DST days come out 23h/25h correctly.
  - Existing DST/timezone tests (Tests/AlmanacCoreTests/TimeModelTests.swift): testDSTSpringForwardDayIsShorterThan24Hours + testDSTFallBackDayIsLongerThan24Hours (Europe/London BST), testEveryDayOfAYearRoundTrips (365-day walk, Asia/Riyadh + wakeOffset — but 2026 is NOT a leap year, so Feb 29 is never exercised), testRiyadhMidnightBoundary, testWakeOffsetPullsSmallHoursIntoPreviousDay.
  - Gaps confirmed: no leap-year test (Feb 29, e.g. 2028), no century-non-leap edge (2100), no half-hour-offset zone (Asia/Kolkata UTC+5:30), no Southern-hemisphere DST (reversed season, e.g. Australia/Sydney), no historical zone-rule-change test.
  - PartialDateTime (Sources/AlmanacCore/Time/PartialDateTime.swift) already regex+Calendar-validates real calendar rollover (rejects Feb 30) — worth a dedicated leap-year-specific test (Feb 29 accepted in leap years, rejected in non-leap years) since it's currently untested for that specific case.

**CI**: none exists. No .github/workflows. This plan cannot add a CI gate that runs on a Mac/Xcode (no such runner is configured) without that being a separate, explicit decision — flag it as optional/out of scope unless the plan proposes a Linux-only `swift test` CI step (which the existing 115 tests already support, since AlmanacCore itself is platform-free).

=== WHAT THE PLAN MUST DECIDE / PRODUCE ===

1. **Data model for hydration**: a new `hydration_log` migration (next number after whatever the current latest migration is — verify by reading Sources/AlmanacCore/Persistence/ and the migration list in code, don't guess the number) modeled on nutrition_log's shape (source_system/external_id identity, logged_at/precision/tz columns via the existing PartialDateTime/ZoneContext types, amount in a real unit type not a bare Double — decide whether to introduce a small Volume/Milliliters wrapper per the Provenance module's "give primitives their own type" pattern already used elsewhere, soft delete, revision table matching the Laboratory pattern only if hydration actually needs edit history — don't over-build if a simpler append-only log suffices, this is a judgement call the plan should make explicitly with reasoning).

2. **HydrationStore / HydrationLoggingService** in Sources/AlmanacCore/Hydration/ — CRUD + TimelineProviding conformance (so it merges into the existing Timeline feed alongside Lab/Health entries), built with the same Clock-injection and Database-wrapper conventions as LabStore/HealthSampleStore. Decide the service's public API surface (log/edit/delete/query methods) concretely, matching call shapes already used by existing stores.

3. **HealthDomain.water (or similarly named) case + write path**: extend the enum, and design how hydration write-back to HealthKit works given HealthProvider is currently read-only — either add a write method to the protocol or a separate small writer protocol, implemented on Linux only as a fake/no-op and for real only in the iOS target's concrete HealthKitProvider.

4. **Offline queue for hydration logging** (mobile-first use case: log water with no network — though note SQLite is local-first already, so clarify what "offline queue" actually means here: is it about queuing HealthKit writes that fail, or queuing a future remote-sync target that doesn't exist yet in this codebase? Ground this in what's actually being synced — check whether there's any remote/server sync elsewhere in the codebase before assuming one, and if there isn't, scope "offline queue/sync recovery" honestly to what exists: HealthKit read/write sync via SyncAnchorStore + HealthSyncService pattern, reusing recordFailure/anchor-preserving semantics) — built on SyncAnchorStore + the transactional read-outside/write-inside pattern from HealthSyncService, not a new mechanism.

5. **Caching + index plan**: given zero caching exists, decide the smallest sensible addition (e.g. a small in-memory LRU or dictionary cache in HydrationStore/NutritionCatalog for hot read paths, or address LabStore's already-flagged range-filtering-in-Swift TODO by pushing it into SQL) rather than a generic caching framework — this should be scoped, not speculative (avoid Speculative Generality). Propose concrete new indexes for hydration_log (time-range query index at minimum, mirroring idx_nutrition_log_time/idx_health_sample_domain_time).

6. **Test plan**: concrete new test files/additions — TimeModelTests leap-year additions (2028 Feb 29, century-non-leap 2100 if relevant to this codebase's range), half-hour-offset zone test (Asia/Kolkata), Southern-hemisphere DST test (Australia/Sydney), a PartialDateTime leap-year validation test; new HydrationStoreTests.swift and HydrationSyncTests.swift/OfflineQueueTests.swift modeled directly on ImportOrderingTests.swift/SyncAndBackupTests.swift patterns cited above.

7. **App target additions** (Native/Almanac/): new files HydrationLoggingView.swift, HydrationDashboardView.swift, SettingsView.swift, and how they get wired into project.pbxproj (note: since there's no Xcode/Mac available to this agent, the plan should specify exact file contents/structure to add AND the precise pbxproj edits needed — PBXBuildFile/PBXFileReference/PBXGroup/PBXSourcesBuildPhase entries — since hand-editing pbxproj is how the existing 4 files got added). Reuse AlmanacApp.swift's existing LaboratoryModel/PartialDateFields/editedDate/EditorFailure patterns for a new HydrationModel or extension of the app's ObservableObject setup. Concrete plan for entitlements file (add com.apple.developer.healthkit) + Info.plist keys (NSHealthShareUsageDescription, NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription) + local-notification authorization request (UNUserNotificationCenter, no Info.plist key required but runtime authorization needed) + the concrete HealthKitProvider: HealthProvider adapter (the one file allowed to `import HealthKit`).

8. **Sequencing**: given this is two efforts that are really one feature, propose a sensible build order (e.g. data layer → core service → tests → HealthKit seam completion → app views → notifications → polish) with rough milestones, not a giant undifferentiated task list.

Produce a concrete, file-by-file implementation plan. Name exact new file paths and, for files being extended, what specifically changes. Do not re-derive the architecture — it's given above; focus on the concrete design decisions (##1-8) and sequencing. Flag any open product questions that need a human decision (e.g. exact hydration units/presets, notification cadence/copy, whether edit history is needed) rather than guessing silently. Keep the plan implementable by someone picking it up fresh.

# Native laboratory manual entry

This is the first iOS app target for the existing Almanac core. It uses the
local package at `../Package.swift`; it adds no server, account system or
separately deployed service. The target supports iPhone and iPad on iOS 17+.

## Authored

- Reports: list, paginate, create, reopen, edit laboratory name and report date.
- Results: canonical/alias search, unmatched source names, create and edit.
- Numeric, qualitative, text, ratio, titer and absent values. Comparators,
  original units, original transcription, laboratory range text/bounds/units,
  reported flags, specimen, method, LOD/LOQ and derivation remain separate.
- Explicit date precision, including Unknown. No device date or timezone is
  filled into a historical result. Existing separately stored zone context
  survives a date edit; textual offsets take precedence in core date queries.
- Report detail, longitudinal test history with source-report navigation, and
  a separate revision history including metadata corrections and attribution.
- Incoming report-conflict review with explicit accept/reject and reason.
  There is no import automation creating these proposals in this app.

The connection is owned on the main actor. Saving an existing result calls the
core's atomic value/metadata edit API. The application uses
`Application Support/Almanac/almanac.sqlite`, migrates in sequence, and seeds
idempotently. An open/migration failure displays an error; it never resets data.
The actor is `user` because this is the existing local personal database model,
not an authenticated multi-user service.

## Verification boundary

The Swift sources pass `swiftc -frontend -parse` on Linux. Project file
references and shared-scheme XML have been checked for internal consistency.
These are **syntax/structure checks, not Apple SDK compilation**.

Not yet verified: SwiftUI type checking against an Apple SDK, Xcode package
resolution and linking, Simulator launch, interactive entry and navigation,
keyboard layout, accessibility, relaunch persistence through the app, device
signing or deployment. Linux core tests do not establish any of these.

## Build and run on a Mac

Open `Native/Almanac.xcodeproj`, select the shared `Almanac` scheme and an
installed iPhone Simulator, then Run. For a command-line Simulator build from
the repository root:

```sh
xcodebuild -project Native/Almanac.xcodeproj -scheme Almanac \
  -configuration Debug -sdk iphonesimulator \
  -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' \
  CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
```

The target has a provisional bundle identifier `com.almanac.personal`. Configure
a suitable identifier/team when preparing a physical-device build. This target
uses no HealthKit capability or document picker.

## Interactive acceptance checks — outstanding

1. Create a report with an unknown date; close and reopen the app and report.
2. Add Hemoglobin, HbA1c, Ferritin, Vitamin D, Creatinine and TSH through alias
   search. Copy original values, units and ranges from test fixtures or a
   report; do not infer a range. Add ANA with qualitative value `Negative`.
3. Add a bounded numeric result using `<`; verify both comparator and original
   transcription appear. Confirm a blank range remains “Not stated”.
4. Enter a month date, date-only, local time with no offset, Z timestamp and
   +03:00 timestamp. Save/reopen each without precision or timezone invention.
   Invalid calendar dates and offsets should display an error and leave data
   unchanged.
5. Edit one value A → B → A, supplying a reason each time. Revision history
   must show three events with only the latest current. Change only specimen
   or collection date and inspect the separate metadata correction record.
6. Add a second report with the same canonical test. Test history must show two
   measurements; their revision histories remain separate. Follow each source
   report link. Different units/specimens remain visible; no combined trend
   curve or unit conversion is inferred.
7. Clear an optional unit/range/date, save and reopen. Confirm the prior value
   is still accessible in history. Cancel an edit and confirm no save occurs.
8. Exercise compact/large Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, iPhone keyboard dismissal
   and iPad navigation. These interaction checks require the actual app.

Report conflict behavior is covered in core tests. To exercise its UI, use a
development fixture that supplies conflicting reports via `upsertReport`; then
accept or reject with a reason and confirm the unresolved badge clears.

Trends, document import, attachments, backup UI, OCR, medical interpretation,
and other tracker screens are outside this pass. The full earlier Laboratory
specification remains incomplete until the remaining features are implemented
and the real UI path above has been verified.
